buy_list.why: Light is the first thing you miss and the cheapest to fix.
Keeps phones alive for days — your lifeline to information.
Clinics may be unreachable; handle the small stuff yourself.
News when the cell network is down.
The core of your 30-day plan; buy on your next grocery run.
Hot food and boiled water without grid power.

meal_ideas: Bean + rice bowls with canned salsa
food.notes: Store what you eat, eat what you store — rotate into normal meals twice a year.

after: Toss perishables above 40°F for 2+ hours (when in doubt, throw it out).
Restock what you used within the week.
Recharge every battery bank before you forget.
Note what worked and what didn't; update this playbook.
before: Charge phones, chargers, and battery banks to 100%.
Fill the bathtub bladder if a storm is forecast.
Turn the fridge and freezer to their coldest settings.
Locate flashlights and test every one.
during: Keep fridge and freezer closed — food stays safe ~4 hours unopened.
Unplug sensitive electronics to avoid surge damage.
Use one room as the 'warm room' at night; close it off.
Never run generators or grills indoors.
Check on neighbors, especially elderly ones.

region_notes: Hurricane season (Jun–Nov): keep the car gassed and documents in a waterproof bag from June onward.
Know your evacuation zone — look it up now, not when the order comes.
Storm surge floods cars first: never drive through water of unknown depth.
After a hurricane, boil-water notices are common — your filter and bleach cover this.

rotation_tips: Mark fill dates with a permanent marker.
Rotate stored tap water every 6 months.
Keep a bottle of unscented bleach for emergency disinfection (8 drops per gallon).

storage_options.detail: Three jugs cover 72 hours; store in a cool closet, rotate every 6 months.
Fill when a storm is forecast — 100 gallons of utility water for flushing and washing.
Simplest start: two 24-packs under a bed.
